referents.why: 'Your hand' is Aaron's: the quoted command is addressed to Aaron.
'Your staff' is Aaron's, as in the quoted command.
'Say to Aaron' is the LORD's command to Moses, so the implied you is Moses, the one commanded. The builder's Aaron is the one spoken to, not the one commanded.
referents.category: implied subject of a command to the speaker

referents.why: 'Stretch out your hand' is in the quoted words, spoken to Aaron.
referents.category: implied you of a quoted command

referents.why: 'Bring up the frogs' is the same quoted command, spoken to Aaron.
referents.category: implied you of a quoted command

links.why: Two commands joined by a waw at one level, same person; the imperative group holds both.
The LORD's saying introduces the telling 'say to Aaron'.
'Tell Aaron' introduces the quoted commands, a collection of commands.

groups.why: The LORD speaks to Moses; the commanded speech Moses gives to Aaron is nested as turn1.
Moses is commanded to tell Aaron, so the words he speaks are his (R2), addressed to Aaron, with the quoted LORD message as its part.
The innermost quoted message is the LORD's and is addressed to Aaron (R2: a message quoting someone else is an innermost turn whose sender is the one quoted).
Stretch out and bring up are commands joined by and at one level: one imperative group with two command members.

none_fit.what: A relayed message has two turns sharing one saying clause (cl1). Nothing in link_types or group_kinds says a turn carries a message that a messenger was told to deliver, beyond the frame reused.
